purpose: Measure bounded fresh logical source admission, recognized-GSO read batching, and sample-free retirement under bidirectional release overload.
kernel: Linux 6.8.0-149-generic #149-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri Oct 23 13:21:10 UTC 2026 x86_64
cpu_model: model name	: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6138 CPU @ 2.00GHz
instrumentation: Ordinary counters only; no timing instrumentation or controller override.
single_lane_harness: benches/tap_transport.sh with only tx_lanes = $workers replaced by tx_lanes = 1; workers and TAP queues remain eight
validation: 349 ordinary release tests, strict all-target Clippy and formatting; 81 kernel tests and all three unchanged runtime tests on Linux 6.8 and 7.0, including allocation assertions. Seven admission regressions include the exact synchronized QinQ burst and excess rejection.

rows.counter_capture_note: Right pre-load daemon log lacks a complete worker snapshot; right daemon counter deltas unavailable. Goodput, CPU, kernel counters and later points are independently captured.

limitations: Single observations at each rate/build in each twenty- and sixty-second sequence; no statistical confidence interval, universal plateau or CPU ceiling is established.
The 2 MiB cap admits the measured 1,071,488-byte burst, but its tuning is not universal and eight-lane pressure remains.
No local builds, kernel tests or Git packing overlapped load tests.
Counter intervals include drain time; CPU spans the active generator interval. Source drops, admission-rejected packets and frame expiry use different units.
Retirement point 0 lacks a complete right pre-load worker snapshot. Its right daemon counter deltas are null, not zero; goodput, CPU and namespace counters remain available.
Fresh admission is the only production candidate selected; read8 and retirement remain isolated patches.

sequences.note: One baseline/candidate/candidate/candidate/baseline sequence with shared controls, not three separate adjacent A/B/A sequences.
Separate instrumented diagnostic; older baseline timing observations are in tap-expiry-timing.json.
Each run offers 4 Gbit/s then unlimited; same source/binaries and limits as the twenty-second tests. Harness now waits for complete worker printouts.
